body_markdown:
**To organize a home library during a renovation or move, sort books and décor, pack reading materials in small, labeled boxes, disassemble or utilize bookshelves, and use self-storage for furniture and items that need to be moved to make space for renovation.** A month-to-month Public Storage rental keeps your timeline flexible as renovation dates, moving schedules, and room setup plans may shift.


A home library renovation or move creates an opportunity to declutter, organize, and refresh your reading space. Start early, pack systematically, and create an inventory that helps you find each box when you are ready to rebuild your shelves.


## **The Basics**


- Clear bookshelves, reading chairs, and non-sensitive reading materials from the room before a renovation or move begins.


- Sort books and décor into categories before packing—


**donate, recycle, gift, and store.**


- Pack books upright in small, sturdy boxes, and label each box by room, shelf, or category.


- Disassemble bookshelves when practical, keep components together, and attach labeled hardware bags to the sets.


- Choose a self-storage unit that fits your library furniture, book boxes, and reading-area décor.


- Use Public Storage’s month-to-month rental agreements to keep your storage timeline flexible to move with renovation delays, moving dates, and the time needed to set up your refreshed space.


- Choose Drive-Up Access for easier loading of bookcases, reading chairs, and heavier boxes.


- Keep a detailed inventory and leave an aisle in your unit so you can find specific books or furniture during the project.


### **Clear Your Home Library Before Work Begins**


**Clearing your home library before a renovation or move begins gives contractors, movers, and you room to work.** Remove books, bookcases, reading chairs, lamps, rugs, and décor from the project area before work starts. A clear area allows renovations to move faster.


Move non-sensitive reading materials and household furnishings into clearly defined groups. Keep personal documents, identification, original contracts, medical records, and other sensitive paperwork out of a self-storage unit.


Set aside a separate box or bag for books you plan to read during the renovation or move. Keep that container in your current living space or vehicle so it remains accessible.


### **Sort Books & Décor Before Packing**


**Sorting books and décor before packing reduces the number of items you move and makes it easier to rebuild an organized library.** Work shelf by shelf instead of emptying the entire room at once. Group books to store by genre, author, room, shelf, or reading status. This approach helps you rebuild your library without opening every box.


**Category & Purpose**


**What To Do**


Donate


Set aside usable books you no longer want for a local organization or book drive


Recycle


Recycle books that local recycling guidance accepts


Gift


Set aside books you want to share with friends, family, or neighbors


Consider gifting books to community “free library” boxes


Store


Pack books, furniture, and décor that you plan to use in your refreshed room


### **Pack Books in Small, Sturdy Boxes**


**Packing books in small, sturdy boxes keeps each box easier to lift, organize, and unpack.** Books tend to be heavy, so weight adds up quickly. Place books upright when they fit, and fill gaps with clean packing paper to limit shifting.


Use these book-packing steps:


- Pack books in smaller boxes instead of oversized containers.


- Keep books from the same shelf or category together.


- Label each box with its room, shelf, or category.


- Write “heavy” on boxes filled with books.


- Seal boxes securely with packing tape.


- Keep a simple inventory list of box labels and contents.


Avoid packing boxes so heavily that they become difficult to lift. Stack heavier book boxes at the bottom of your self-storage unit and lighter containers on top.


### **Disassemble or Utilize Furniture**


**Disassembling bookshelves and reading furniture saves space and makes larger items easier to move.** Remove adjustable shelves, detachable legs, and other components when practical.


Keep each furniture set together:


- Place screws, brackets, shelf pins, and tools in labeled bags.


- Attach the labeled hardware bag to the matching bookshelf or furniture piece.


- Bundle removable shelves together.


- Cover bookcases, chairs, and tables with moving blankets, furniture covers, or clean sheets.


- Label each larger piece with the room where it belongs.


Take photos before disassembly. Photos help you remember shelf placement, furniture arrangement, and décor layouts when you rebuild your library.


You may also choose to use the bookshelves as a form of organization inside the unit. An organized storage unit makes visits to locate specific books less stressful.


### **Choose a Unit Size & Features for Your Home Library Storage**


**Choosing a self-storage unit for your home library starts with measuring bookcases, reading chairs, tables, and the number of packed book boxes.** The right unit size depends on how much furniture and how many shelves you need to clear to make room for your renovation or clear during your move.


**Unit Size & Library Storage Need**


**Typical Fit**


**5′ x 5′**


Book boxes, lamps, décor, and smaller reading-area items


**5′ x 10′**


Book boxes, a reading chair, and furniture from a small library or office


**10′ x 10′**


Multiple bookcases, chairs, book boxes, and furniture from several areas


**10′ x 15′ or Larger**


Larger home-library furniture, extensive book collections, and multi-room renovation items

### **Keep Your Storage Timeline Flexible**


**Public Storage’s month-to-month agreements allow you to utilize a self-storage unit for your home-library during a renovation or move and be flexible if construction or the move take longer than expected.** Renovation schedules, contractor availability, paint drying, flooring installation, furniture delivery, and move-in dates often change, so your agreement can extend or end as needed.


Public Storage offers month-to-month rental agreements, so you can rent storage while work continues and end the rental after you set up your refreshed reading space.


### **Organize Your Unit for Easy Access**


**Organizing your self-storage unit for easy access helps you find books, furniture, and décor during the project.** Place items you expect to retrieve first near the entrance, and leave a clear aisle from the door to the back wall if you expect you’ll need to access items during storage.


Follow this layout:


- Put bookcases and heavier furniture along the unit walls.


- Stack heavy book boxes on the floor.


- Place lighter bins and décor boxes on top or on shelving.


- Group boxes from the same room or shelf together.


- Keep a detailed inventory list and a simple map of the unit.


- Leave an aisle wide enough to reach stored items.


This layout helps you retrieve a specific box or furniture piece without unpacking the entire unit.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


**How Do I Organize My Home Library Before a Renovation?**


You organize your home library before a renovation by clearing furniture and non-sensitive reading materials from the room, sorting books into donate, recycle, gift, and store categories, and packing stored books in labeled boxes. Work shelf by shelf to keep the process organized.


**How Should I Pack My Books for a Move or Renovation?**


You should pack your books for a move or renovation in small, sturdy boxes labeled by room, shelf, or category. Pack books upright when they fit, avoid overfilling boxes, and stack heavier book boxes on the bottom during storage.


**What Size Self-Storage Unit Do I Need for My Home Library?**


You should choose a self-storage unit for your home library by measuring bookcases and furniture, counting boxes, and considering how often you plan to access the unit. A 5′ x 5′ unit fits boxes and smaller items easily, while a 5′ x 10′ or 10′ x 10′ unit fits more furniture and a larger book collection. Review the


[Public Storage Size Guide](https://www.publicstorage.com/size-guide) for more options.


**Should I Choose Drive-Up Access for My Home Library Move?**


You should choose Drive-Up Access for your home library move when you need to load bookcases, reading chairs, tables, and heavier book boxes. Drive-Up Access places your vehicle near select ground-level units and streamlines loading and unloading.


**How Long Can I Rent Storage During My Library Renovation?**


You can rent storage during your library renovation for as long as your project requires through Public Storage’s month-to-month rental agreements. This flexibility supports shifting renovation schedules, moving dates, and the time needed to organize your completed space.
